solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See a punch I swung, angry? My arm-ends are balled (13, two words)

indicators.note: something swung is moved about out of its resting place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see
taken as written, to be mixed with the letter before
cross means annoyed or angry

explanation.surface: Someone throws a wild, angry punch while bragging that their fists are clenched into balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross itself speaking: in heraldry a capuchin cross has a ball at the end of each arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A capuchin cross is a heraldic cross whose four limbs each terminate in a ball, so its arm-ends are balled.

clue.text: American plant seen in two states briefly

indicators.note: briefly asks for the short, abbreviated forms of the words in question

blocks.note: first state: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
second state: Mass. is the short form of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a certain American plant grows in two US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Camass is a North American plant of the lily family whose bulbs were eaten by Native Americans.

clue.text: Eaterie, reverse of old-style? soup he ordered is taken outside

indicators.note: reverse of tells us to write the following word backwards
ordered means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged
something taken outside goes round the other piece and encloses it

blocks.note: retro means imitating an old style
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic sniffs at a retro place where the customer orders soup to take away.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled soup and he wrap around the backwards word; the question mark admits the surface is strained.
explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse was originally a tavern serving porter ale and chops or steaks, so it is an eating house.

clue.text: German dish, accompaniment for soup, not available?

indicators.note: not marks letters to be removed, and available means on, as in a dish on the menu

blocks.note: a croûton is a cube of fried bread served in soup

explanation.surface: A diner is told the croutons for the soup have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ON (available) from the end of the soup accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: Crout is a variant of sauerkraut, the shredded pickled cabbage of German cooking.

clue.text: What'll sell takeaway (no starter) for dropout?

indicators.note: with no starter, the first letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a chippie is a British fish-and-chip shop, selling takeaway food

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what kind of takeaway food would suit someone who has dropped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course from the takeaway menu, but it means the first letter of the shop's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippie is someone who has rejected conventional society, the classic dropout of the 1960s counterculture.

clue.text: Toughens a lens that's cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Glassmakers harden a lens that has developed a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: To neal is an old form of anneal, hardening glass or metal by heating and slow cooling.

clue.text: Paint company surmounting gloomy appearance

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a lour is a frown or gloomy look

explanation.surface: A paint firm's logo is placed above a sullen-looking display.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, surmounting puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour as a verb means to apply paint or pigment to something.

clue.text: Took part in boat race in sound course

indicators.note: in sound means we go by how the word is pronounced, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: someone who took part in a boat race rowed

explanation.surface: A rower recalls taking part in a boat race on a good, healthy course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (a sound course) but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a way or route, which is one sense of course.

clue.text: The rotor pin goes wrong in unlikely flyer

indicators.note: when something goes wrong it falls into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A helicopter's rotor pin fails, causing trouble in an improbable aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornithopter is a machine designed to fly by flapping wings like a bird, which has rarely worked.

clue.text: Ear canal, one below top of head mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, below sends the first-named piece underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: the scalp is the skin covering the top of the head
a means one

explanation.surface: An anatomy note placing an ear canal below the top of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one placed below the shortened scalp follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scala is one of the spiral canals of the cochlea in the inner ear.

clue.text: Re gland, see two adjacent parts transposed in a pig's

indicators.note: transposing two adjacent parts swaps a neighbouring pair of letters, a tiny rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
porcine means of or relating to pigs

explanation.surface: A note about a pig's gland, telling the reader to see where two parts have been switched.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the third and fourth letters of the word for a pig's.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocrine describes a type of gland that loses part of its cells in secreting, so it is an adjective concerning glands.

clue.text: Bridge builder restructured one pronto

indicators.note: restructured means built again in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge-building firm hurriedly redesigns something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontooner is a soldier or worker who builds pontoon bridges from floating supports.

clue.text: Newcomer joining table turned up in vain taking in a point

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
taking in means admitting something inside, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: a no-go effort is one that comes to nothing
taken as written
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a table but, turned away, tries in vain to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' is the periodic table. No-go, as in a no-go effort, means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Oganesson, element 118, was named in 2016, one of the newest additions to the periodic table.

clue.text: Jam may result in this content of plum or apricot

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what lies inside it, letters running across its words

blocks.note: the letters run across the words plum, or and apricot

explanation.surface: A cook explains that jam can be made from the flesh of plums or apricots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' suggests fruit preserve; here it is a traffic jam, and what results is a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mora is a delay, especially a culpable one in law, and a traffic jam causes delay.

clue.text: Aromatic rhizome left on dipping in dippy

indicators.note: dipping in means plunging inside, so these pieces go within the next word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an is an old form of on
gaga means silly or senile

explanation.surface: A dippy cook dunks some aromatic root into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed takes AN as an archaic form of on, found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Galanga, or galangal, is the aromatic underground stem of a plant of the ginger family, used in cooking.

clue.text: Peanuts, singularly wretched pay (6, two words)

indicators.note: something wretched is in a poor state, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the singular of peanuts

explanation.surface: A worker complains that their wages are peanuts, miserable pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peanuts' in the surface is slang for a tiny wage; here it is just letters, used singly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ante up is to pay what is owed or contribute one's share, from putting a stake into a poker pot.

clue.text: Look within a visage? it's lacking presence of feudal lord

indicators.note: within places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a + dial, slang for the face
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a face and notices it has no lordly bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dial is British slang for a person's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Alodial land is held outright, free from any rent or service owed to an overlord, unlike feudal tenure.

clue.text: Restore revenue in Polish city

blocks.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to restore a deleted passage
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A council aims to restore tax revenue in a Polish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Stettin is the German name of Szczecin, a port in north-west Poland.

clue.text: Alcohol burns within this wheeling part of flagrant experiment

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is taken
wheeling means turning round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A reckless lab experiment where spirits catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Etna' tempts as the volcano, but here it is the small heating vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An etna is a small vessel for heating liquids, with a saucer of burning spirit underneath it.

clue.text: Metallic element in measure of land, rather scattered around (9, two words)

indicators.note: scattered letters are spread about, so they are put back in a new order
around means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
an are is a metric unit of land area, 100 square metres

explanation.surface: A metal is found in a plot of land, rather widely dispersed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare earth is any of the lanthanide metals, a group of metallic elements.

clue.text: Make a new arrangement for holiday destination?

blocks.note: first meaning: to sort again
second meaning: a place people go on holiday

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as booking a holiday; the first meaning is the verb split as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-sort means to sort again into a new order, and a resort is a place visited for holidays.

clue.text: Primates as a group apparently leading way heavenward

indicators.note: leading picks out the opening letters of the word it follows
in a down clue, heavenward means going upwards, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the leading letters of apparently
a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: Apes as a group seemingly point the way towards heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, two leading letters are taken. 'Primates' looks like churchmen, which suits heavenward, but means apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Apedom is apes collectively, the world or condition of apes.

clue.text: Water rising in channel sounded warning?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a river's bed is the channel it flows in
to pee is to pass water

explanation.surface: Rising water in a channel set off an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' is not the river but a verb, to urinate. The question mark flags that beeping need not be a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeped means made a short electronic sound, as an alarm or horn does to warn.

clue.text: Salmon in small boat, heated, trimmed in the same way

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, and in the same way applies the same cut, the last letter, to both words

blocks.note: a cog is a small boat, also called a cock-boat
something heated is hot

explanation.surface: A salmon is cooked in a little boat, trimmed of its fins.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a Pacific salmon, also called the silver salmon.

clue.text: Times of repose or constant relief

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
alms are relief given to the poor

explanation.surface: Choosing between periods of rest and constant relief from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Calms are periods of stillness and quiet, such as windless spells at sea.

clue.text: Time to drain all but last incline

indicators.note: all but last keeps every letter except the final one

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: It is time to drain everything except the last of a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' looks like a slope, but it is the verb, to make someone inclined.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or dispose someone towards something, the verb sense of incline.

clue.text: Remove intervening spaces, being intimate

blocks.note: first meaning: a printer's instruction to bring the parts together
second meaning: at very close quarters

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is usually phrased the other way round as close up, a proofreader's mark for closing a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To close up type is to remove the gaps, while up close means at very close range or on intimate terms.

clue.text: Couple finally changing places in sign of approval embrace

indicators.note: the final couple of letters change places with each other, a two-letter rearrangement

blocks.note: an audience claps to show approval

explanation.surface: A couple at last swap seats and embrace, to approving applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp is to hold tightly in the arms, which is to embrace.

clue.text: Denials in the main rebuffed inexplicable feelings

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the word runs backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the main is a literary term for the open sea
noes are refusals or denials

explanation.surface: Refusals at sea, pushed back, leave sailors with feelings they cannot explain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoesis is sensation or feeling without any understanding of it, so anoeses are feelings not grasped by the intellect.

clue.text: Fine chefs will include this traditional supplement

indicators.note: to include something is to contain it, here inside the letters of the preceding words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Good chefs always add a classic side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Traditional flags an old word; supplement is a verb, to add to.
explanation.definitionFit: Eche is an archaic form of eke, meaning to increase or add to something, so to supplement it.

clue.text: Losing heart she goes after bloodless turns, passing

indicators.note: turns means the word faces the other way, so it is read backwards
losing heart means the middle letter is taken out
goes after means this piece is placed second, following the other

blocks.note: someone bloodless is pale
taken as written, then its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: A heartbroken woman, pale and turning, is passing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Elapse as a noun is the passing of time, matching passing as a noun.

clue.text: Eye condition, form of macule round front of optic

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of the next word
a form of a word is that word given a new shape, so its letters are rearranged
round means encircling, as the reshaped letters take in the extra one

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
the first letter of optic

explanation.surface: An eye disease taking the form of a spot around the front of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A macule is itself a spot on the skin, which makes the surface read as medical.
explanation.definitionFit: Leucoma is a white opaque scar on the cornea of the eye.

clue.text: Crowning vegetable to cut back

indicators.note: cut means removed, here a two-letter word named in the clue
back means the remainder is written backwards

blocks.note: a potato is a vegetable
the word to itself is what gets cut

explanation.surface: A vegetable crowning a dish is to be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' reads as part of the instruction, but the word to is literally removed from the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on the top of, the position of a crown.

clue.text: One pegs out inhaling hot toxic gas

indicators.note: inhaling means drawing something inside, so one letter goes within the rest
out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
H stands for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone dies after breathing in a hot poisonous gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pegs out' looks like the idiom for dies, but out alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a poisonous gas, carbonyl chloride, used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: Amiable Sandy's idle, having met pet playing inside

indicators.note: playing means moving about freely, so these letters are rearranged
inside places one piece within the other
having means holding, so the first piece contains the second

blocks.note: sweered is Scots for lazy or reluctant; Sandy is a stock Scotsman
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A good-natured, lazy Scot met a pet that was playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandy' is a stock name for a Scot, so Sandy's word is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-tempered describes someone of a gentle, good-natured disposition, which is to say amiable.
